html.body: Date: 2025-03-31 INTERVIEW SUMMARYApplicant thanks Examiner Sienko for the interview conducted on March 28, 2025.During the interview, proposed claim amendments and cited references were discussed. The Examiner indicated that the proposed claim amendments would warrant further search. The proposed claim amendments and additional amendments are submitted herein.REMARKSThe foregoing amendments and the remarks that follow are meant to impart precision to the claims, and more particularly point out the invention, rather than to avoid prior art.Claims 1-20 are pending in the application. Claims 1-6 and 11-20 were rejected. Claims 7-10 were objected to. Claims 1, 3, 11, 13, 16, and 18 are amended. No new matter has been added.35 U.S.C. §§ 102, 103 Claims 1-2, 4, 11-12, and 14 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2019/0113926 to Sim ("Sim"). Claim 3 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 1, in view of PCT Publication No. 2021/239531 to Maurer et al. ("Maurer"). Claim 5 was rejected under 35 U.S.C.§ 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 1, in view of U.S. Publication No. 2021/0001888 to Oguro et al. ("Oguro"), in further view of D.E. Publication No.202019005277 to Zhikhareva ("Zhikhareva"), and in further view of NPL "Rettungsgasse lnfovideo - So Funktioniert die Rettungsgasse" ("Rettungsgasse"). Claim 6 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 1, in view of U.S.Publication No. 2022/0063495 to Hawley et al. ("Hawley"). Claim 13 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 11, in view of Maurer.Claim 15 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 11, in view of Oguro and Zhikhareva, and in further view of Rettungsgasse.Claims 16-17, and 19-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim, in view of Oguro. Claim 18 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Sim as applied to claim 16, in view of Maurer.Applicant respectfully traverses all of the rejections.The Cited References Fail To Disclose: "determining, by the computing system, map data associated with the environment, wherein the map data includes information associated with a presence of an emergency lane that is different from a rescue lane" Without conceding the correctness of the rejections, the claims have been amended to advance prosecution. As amended, claim 1 recites, inter alia, "determining, by the computing system, map data associated with the environment, wherein the map data includes information associated with a presence of an emergency lane that is different from a rescue lane." Claims 11 and 16 recite similar claim features. The cited references fail to disclose at least these instant claim features.In support of the rejection of the claims, the Office Action cites, inter alia, Maurer. Office Action, 6. Maurer relates to an emergency lane assistant. The Abstract of Maurer provides as follows:The invention relates to a method forforming an emergency lane (14) for a vehicle (10), wherein the vehicle (10) has at least one surroundings sensor (16, 18, 20) for capturing surroundings (22) of the vehicle (10), comprising the steps of detecting a driving situation on a road (32) comprising a roadway (34) having a plurality of traffic lanes (36) for a direction of travel (38) of the vehicle (10), ascertaining a congestion situation on the road (32), detecting a traffic lane (36) being travelled in by the vehicle (10) from the plurality of traffic lanes (36) for the direction of travel (38) of the vehicle (10), detecting a position of the vehicle (10) with respect to surrounding vehicles (44) and/or one or more boundaries (40, 42) of traffic lanes (36) and/or the roadway (34) based on sensor information provided by the at least one surroundings sensor (16, 18, 20), determining a required change in position of the vehicle (10) in order to form the emergency lane (14) based on the traffic lane (36) being travelled in by the vehicle (10) and the position of the vehicle (10) with respect to surrounding vehicles (44) and/or one or more boundaries (40, 42) of traffic lanes (36) and/or the roadway (34), and outputting the required change in position of the vehicle (10) in order to form the emergency lane (14). The invention furthermore relates to a driver assistance system (12) that is designed to perform the above method.Maurer, Abstract (emphasis added). Importantly, Maurer's reference to an "emergency lane" is in the context offormation of the emergency lane.With respect to the instant claim features, a portion of which were previously recited in claim 3, the Office Action cites certain portions of Maurer. Office Action, 7. The cited portions of Maurer include the following excerpts:In an advantageous embodiment of the invention, detecting a driving situation on a road with a lane with multiple lanes for one direction of travel of the vehicle includes determining a vehicle position based on received satellite position signals from a global navigation satellite system and detecting the driving situation based on driving situation information associated with the vehicle position. The global navigation satellite system (GNSS) satellite position signals indicate an absolute position of the vehicle on the earth's surface. The driving situation information can be part of map information which is used for navigation and which includes information about a number oflanesfor possible driving directions. The driving situation information can be stored locally in the vehicle, in particular in a memory of the driving support system.Maurer, 11 (emphasis added). Here, Maurer has a limited reference to map information in relation to a number of lanes of a road. In relevant part, Maurer stops there.Maurer also discusses lane detection. In a portion cited by the Office Action, Maurer provides as follows:... Step S120 relates to a detection of a lane 36 traveled by the vehicle 10 from the multiple lanes 36 for the direction of travel 38 of the vehicle 10. Based on the detection of the lane 36 traveled by the vehicle 10, a positionfor the emergency lane 14 to be formed can be determined. The lane 36 traveled by the vehicle 10 is detected from the multiple lanes 36 for the direction of travel 38 of the vehicle 10, preferably based on sensor information provided by the environmental sensors 16, 18, 20. Alternatively or additionally, the lane 36 traveled by the vehicle 10 can be determined based on received satellite navigation data.Maurer, 12 (emphasis added). Here, Maurer references detection of a lane based on sensor information from environmental sensors. This reference in Maurer is unrelated to a map. In addition, Maurer reiterates once again that the "emergency lane" in the Maurer system is not preexisting but rather is affirmatively formed.Maurer fails to disclose the instant claim features. First, as discussed, Maurer is entirely bereft of any suggestion of an emergency lane as claimed. The claimed emergency lane 1) is different from the claimed rescue lane and 2) is not the "emergency lane" that needs to be formed in Maurer. Second, while Maurer in passing discusses map information in relation to a number of lanes, Maurer fails to disclose map data that includes information about the claimed emergency lane. Accordingly, Maurer does not disclose determining, by the computing system, map data associated with the environment, wherein the map data includes information associated with a presence of an emergency lane that is different from a rescue lane, as claimed.The other cited references do not remedy the deficiencies of Maurer.Thus, claims 1, 11, and 16, and their dependent claims, are patentable for at least these reasons.CONCLUSIONAccordingly, the independent claims are patentable. The dependent claims are patentable both by their dependence on patentable independent claims and in their own right. While all of the Examiner's rejections are respectfully traversed, it is submitted that the foregoing reasons are sufficient to demonstrate the patentability of the pending claims without addressing any remaining rejections.It is respectfully submitted that all of the Examiner's rejections have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in order for allowance. Accordingly, reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is courteously solicited.Authorization is hereby given to charge our Deposit Account No. 50-4561 for any charges that may be due and/or credit any overpayments. Furthermore, if an extension is required, then such an extension is hereby requested.Respectfully submitted, Date: March 31, 2025 By: /James W. Soong/ James W. Soong, Reg.
